name: WordPress
note: Enumerate the version (readme.html, meta generator) and installed plugins/themes; check both against known CVEs.

name: Drupal
note: Check /CHANGELOG.txt and /core/CHANGELOG.txt for the version; Drupal has had several critical unauthenticated RCEs (Drupalgeddon).

name: Joomla
note: Check /administrator/manifests/files/joomla.xml for the version and cross-reference known CVEs.

name: Apache HTTP Server
note: Confirm the version from the Server header and check for known CVEs; consider whether mod_status/server-status is exposed.

name: Nginx
note: Confirm the version and review the reverse-proxy config for exposed internal upstreams or default server blocks.

name: Microsoft IIS
note: Check for legacy IIS shortname enumeration (~) and known ASP.NET deserialization CVEs matching the disclosed version.

name: PHP
note: Note the disclosed PHP version; cross-reference against the PHP end-of-life/CVE list.

name: Express (Node.js)
note: Confirm default Express security middleware (helmet, rate limiting) is in use; Express sets few security headers by default.

name: Django
note: If a debug/traceback page is reachable, DEBUG=True may be enabled in production, which leaks source and settings.

name: ASP.NET
note: Check whether ViewState MAC validation is enabled; unauthenticated ViewState deserialization has led to critical RCEs.

name: React
note: Client-rendered SPA — enumerate the compiled JS bundle for embedded API routes, feature flags, and secrets.

name: Cloudflare
note: Traffic is proxied through a CDN/WAF; direct-origin discovery becomes a relevant recon step for bypassing edge protections.
